title: Hydrological regime is associated with environmental and spatial signals in zooplankton metacommunity structure across taxonomic groups in a neotropical floodplain
content:
ABSTRACT
Hydrological variation in river–floodplain systems is associated with changes in environmental heterogeneity and dispersal-related processes. Using data from a 15-year monitoring program in the Upper Paraná River floodplain, we quantified the environmental and spatial fractions of zooplankton community variation across taxonomic groups and contrasting hydrological periods. Patterns associated with metacommunity organization varied consistently among zooplankton groups along the hydrological cycle. As river level increased, fine-scale spatial fractions compatible with mass effects became more evident, especially during high-water periods, suggesting increased spatial signals associated with dispersal among habitats. In contrast, during low-water conditions, environmental fractions consistent with species sorting were generally higher, particularly for smaller-bodied taxa. However, cladocerans exhibited a non-linear response, with higher environmental factors contributing at intermediate water levels. Large-scale spatial fractions consistent with dispersal limitation were more evident for copepods during low-water periods, suggesting increased spatial constraints under reduced connectivity. Overall, our results indicate that hydrological variation is associated with shifts in environmental and spatial signals in zooplankton metacommunities, and these signals differ among taxonomic groups.
